name: KERF

intro.problem: Two parts of the analysis rest on densities that are never modeled explicitly. The ABCD background estimate assumes its two discriminants factorize, which fails when they are correlated, most of all in sparse tails [@choi2021]. The networks learn each feature's evidence from scratch, which is hardest where events are few.
intro.value: Maximum entropy gives both a principled form [@jaynes1957]. A background model that learns the dependence, rather than removing it during training [@abcdisco2021][@cms2025tec], turns non-closure into a measured and correctable quantity. Per-feature signal and background densities hand the networks each feature's evidence, with the quality of every model graded.
intro.approach: KERF fits maximum-entropy marginals once and builds on them twice. For background, an exponential tilt chosen by kernel maximal correlation [@renyi1959][@huang2020], extended to a kernel exponential family [@sriperumbudur2017], is scored on closure. For signal, cross-fitted per-feature likelihood ratios across all mass points [@chernozhukov2018] become network inputs, each model graded for goodness and leakage.
intro.goals: Two deliverables: an improved, and potentially novel, data-driven background estimate with honest uncertainties, benchmarked against extended and Bayesian ABCD methods [@choi2021][@alvarez2024]; and a graded likelihood-ratio input layer, tested against the networks' current inputs where statistics are thinnest.

questions: Can a kernel-chosen dependence term recover the correlation that a factorized estimate misses, especially in the sparse tail where the signal region sits?
Can a flexible background model stay honest: closing on held-out regions without absorbing injected signal?

Can per-feature maximum-entropy evidence, with every model's goodness and leakage measured and the mass points pooled, mixed, kept apart or conditioned on mass, give the networks inputs that beat rank scaling on separation or closure, most of all where statistics are thin?

timeline.label: MaxEnt background model specified: product of fitted marginals plus dependence rungs
First MaxEnt ladder run: product baseline, Gaussian copula, and mixture copula rungs
Second-generation MaxEnt planned; literature and novelty check
Kernel MaxEnt plan locked: kernel-selected dependence term, gated test plan, genealogy deck
Kernel models explored for the low-statistics barrel region
Formalized as its own project and named KERF
Dependence probe added: learned two-sample test of real background against the factorized product and against each joint-model rung
Signal variant specified: conditional maximum-entropy signal model built from all simulated mass points
Signal line redefined: per-feature maximum-entropy likelihood-ratio inputs with goodness and leakage scorecards, replacing the joint signal model
Private repository created; first signal-evidence code: per-feature densities, nested cross-fitting, scorecards, leave-one-mass-out and a correlation-free reference classifier
Outline rewritten as five programs; equal-weight pooled and mass-conditioned signal densities added to the signal code
Signal evidence: data wiring, then first real-data scorecards in both regions
Gate thresholds locked before any benchmark run uses the verdicts
Folds shared with the benchmark, then likelihood-ratio input variants against the rank-scaled control
Background rungs ported onto the shared marginal engine and refitted on the current background sample
Dependence probe: real background against the shuffled product, full plane and corner, then against each rung
Gated tests: toy harness, structure check, blinded toy closure, held-out corners, signal injection

links.title: Applied in the barrel program
links.text: The barrel is the region where a factorized estimate is least trustworthy and statistics are thinnest. STAVE applies this joint-background model there and scores it against the shared barrel baseline. The per-feature input layer is expected to matter most there, where networks have too few events to learn each feature's transform themselves.

links.title: Latent version of the probe
links.text: The same two-sample idea applied to the networks' hidden layers, to see where dependence lives before it reaches the scores.

links.title: Preprocessing axis in the benchmark
links.text: The likelihood-ratio input variants run as cells beside the current rank scaling, scored with the benchmark's own separation and closure measures.

tagline: Maximum-entropy and kernel models of background and signal: the dependence behind the background estimate, and graded per-feature evidence for the networks

components.name: MaxEnt synthetic background
components.subtitle: Program 1 · the first model
components.summary: Per-feature marginals fitted to the total background, sampled as a product (plain ABCD), then with Gaussian and mixture copulas added as dependence rungs [@jaynes1957]. The marginal engine is shared with the signal program, so both sides of the analysis use one density model.

items.label: Rungs
items.detail: Product, Gaussian copula, mixture copula; each set of draws is pushed through the frozen networks to rebuild every ABCD region

items.label: Refit
items.detail: Ported onto the shared marginal engine and refitted on the current background sample before the kernel rungs are compared with it

components.name: Kernel dependence
components.subtitle: Program 2 · let the data choose the constraint
components.summary: Keep the marginals fixed and model the linking term as an exponential tilt. Kernel maximal correlation picks the functions [@renyi1959][@huang2020]; distance correlation is itself a kernel statistic, which ties this to the decorrelation line [@sejdinovic2013]. A density-ratio critic is an alternative route to the same term [@vandenoord2018].

items.label: Tilt
items.detail: One kernel-chosen pair of functions; plain ABCD is the case where the tilt is zero

items.label: Full family
items.detail: A kernel exponential family with the truncation removed, only if the tilt leaves structure behind [@sriperumbudur2017]

items.label: Tail bases
items.detail: Kernels that revert to factorization in the corner are avoided where the signal region sits

components.name: Dependence probe
components.subtitle: Program 3 · a learned test of what the joint model missed
components.summary: A classifier two-sample test [@lopezpaz2017] on background only. Real background pairs of the two feature blocks are set against the same pairs with one block shuffled, which is exactly the factorized product. A network that lets one block attend to the other [@vaswani2017] is the critic; if it cannot beat chance, there is no dependence for any model to recover. The same critic then sets real background against draws from each joint-model rung.

items.label: Ladder
items.detail: Real against product, then real against each rung (copulas, kernel tilt, full family); a rung that captures the dependence drives the critic toward chance

items.label: Corner
items.detail: A version restricted to the high-score corner, where a global dependence measure is dominated by the bulk and the signal region sits

items.label: Level
items.detail: Run on the features the joint model fits; if the model is fitted on scores, the probe moves to scores

items.label: Scope
items.detail: Attention crosses the two feature blocks only inside this background-only diagnostic and never feeds a classifier, consistent with the token line's rule

items.label: Related
items.detail: A neural estimate of mutual information is the continuous counterpart of the same question [@belghazi2018]

items.label: Labeling
items.detail: Model draws and real background stay in separate, labeled runs; no reported real-data quantity uses model draws

components.name: Per-feature MaxEnt signal evidence
components.subtitle: Program 4 · a likelihood-ratio input layer for the networks
components.summary: For every network input feature, one-dimensional maximum-entropy densities are fitted to background and to signal built from all simulated mass points [@jaynes1957]. Each feature is then replaced by, or paired with, its log-likelihood ratio before it reaches the network: a fixed, supervised preprocessing stage the current networks do not have. Events, labels and the training loop are unchanged; the network still learns from true labels and is left to learn how the features combine. Every density carries a goodness and leakage scorecard, and a feature whose model fails keeps its plain input.

items.label: Densities
items.detail: Maximum entropy under Legendre moment constraints, on one coordinate shared by every density of a feature so the Jacobian cancels in the ratio; discrete features live on their support points and a frequent single value becomes a point mass

items.label: Constraints
items.detail: The number of constraints is chosen inside each fit's own events, never on an evaluation fold

items.label: Mass handling
items.detail: Six options built and compared: one fit to all mass points with size or equal weights, size- and equal-weighted mixtures of per-mass fits, one channel per mass point, and a mass-conditioned density for a parameterized network [@baldi2016]

items.label: Labels
items.detail: Labels stay as sample provenance and are never re-assigned from model probabilities; the models change only the inputs, and their densities are never sampled to make training events

items.label: Cross-fitting
items.detail: Nested: a training event's input comes from a model that saw neither the event nor the outer held-out fold; in-sample inputs are kept only as the leakage control [@chernozhukov2018]

items.label: Replace or augment
items.detail: Each variant runs with the ratio replacing the feature and alongside it, since a non-monotone ratio folds a feature and can lose information

items.label: Control
items.detail: The current rank-scaled inputs; every variant is judged against them on separation, worst mass point and closure

items.label: Goodness
items.detail: Held-out likelihood gain over a two-moment fit and a histogram, calibration of the whole distribution and of each tail by the probability integral transform [@gneiting2007], share of events outside the fitted range, fold-to-fold stability of the ratio, and its reliability against observed odds

items.label: Leakage
items.detail: In-sample against held-out likelihood gap for every density, and the separation lost when a network is trained on cross-fitted rather than in-sample inputs

items.label: Gates
items.detail: Pass thresholds are proposed in advance and locked before any benchmark run uses the verdicts; choosing them after seeing which features pass would be selection on the outcome

items.label: Interpolation
items.detail: Leave-one-mass-out for every option that combines mass points, the mass-conditioned density included; it must beat reusing the nearest mass point

items.label: Diagnostic
items.detail: The sum of the per-feature ratios is a classifier that ignores correlations; the network's gain over it measures what correlations contribute

components.name: Gated tests
components.subtitle: Program 5 · earn each step before the next
components.summary: Toy harness, structure diagnosis, blinded toy closure, held-out pseudo-signal regions on real background, then signal injection to check the background model does not absorb signal. Injected events are real simulated signal, tagged and never counted as extra statistics.
